open_obligations: Note that the result is a theoretical protocol, not an observation of obfuscation in practice.
Check that the rho-stability assumption holds for the harder questions Michael et al. have in mind.
Note Michael et al.'s free-text debates are not recursive, unlike the protocol.
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Michael et al. say future work should monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle on harder questions. Brown-Cohen et al. propose prover-estimator debate, which under stability assumptions lets an honest debater win with computation comparable to its opponent, mitigating obfuscation; the result is theoretical and gives no empirical evidence on whether obfuscation arises.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether obfuscated arguments can be prevented in recursive debate, in a complexity-theoretic model with stability assumptions

text: The authors report that they do not observe obfuscated arguments to be a significant problem in their setting, noting differences from the OpenAI physics debates (recursive structure, no evidence grounding or judge interaction, small-scale tricky questions). They state that future work running debates on harder questions can monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle in practice.
title: Will obfuscated arguments become an obstacle for debate on harder questions?
